extracted.intended_audience: legislators, patent practitioners, inventors, corporate counsel, and other patent-system stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and policy goals articulated in Senate debate about the America Invents Act, describing what constitutes valid priority, prior art, PTO procedures, enforcement reforms, and measures to improve patent quality and reduce litigation and backlog. Useful for evaluating or implementing patent-law reforms and related PTO practice changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-inventor-to-file priority (priority determined by filing date)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transition from first-to-invent to a first-inventor-to-file system in which the filing date determines priority rather than an earlier date of conception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under first to file, once the inventor files information with the Patent Office, he has a priority date that is both secure and public. The filing date is what will determine priority, not a purported date of conception, making it much harder for thieves to claim earlier invention dates. This harmonizes U.S. practice with the rest of the world and provides greater certainty for innovators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of provisional applications to secure priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow inventors to file informal and inexpensive provisional applications that need only disclose what the invention is and how to make it, thereby securing a public priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional applications are inexpensive and need only disclose information the inventor already has; once filed they create a secure, public priority date and reduce need for expensive litigation to establish invention dates. The text also notes that a provisional application constitutes section 103 prior art as of its filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public-availability standard for prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Redefine 'prior art' so that public uses and sales are prior art only if they make the invention available to the public; confidential sales, private demonstrations, or private third-party use do not constitute prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limiting prior art to activities that make the invention publicly accessible reduces the need for depositions and discovery to uncover secret dealings and greatly reduces time and cost of patent litigation. It makes validation of prior art rely on publicly accessible information rather than private activities that are easier to fake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of a grace period protecting inventors' disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain an important grace period so that inventors (especially universities and small inventors) can publicly disclose their inventions without automatically losing rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the bill, once a U.S. inventor publicly discloses his invention, no third party’s application filed after that date can be valid because filing date determines priority. The inventor can disclose in academic papers and at trade shows without worrying that such disclosures will lead to theft or fraudulent invalidation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party participation during examination (pre-issuance comments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow third parties to comment on pending patent applications so patent examiners have more and better information readily available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expanding the role of third parties in the examination process is intended to improve patent quality by providing examiners with additional prior art or critiques that could prevent issuance of low-quality patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-grant review to weed out recently issued bad patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement a streamlined postgrant review process (a 'first-window' postgrant review) to quickly challenge and eliminate patents that should not have been issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This implements a National Academy of Sciences recommendation and provides a timely administrative alternative to district court litigation to address improperly granted patents, improving overall patent quality and certainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reform of inter partes reexamination (improve administrative challenge process)
rubrics_metrics.description: Change the existing inter partes reexamination process, which had been criticized as too easy to initiate and too lengthy, to provide a more effective, timely administrative mechanism for challenging patent validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The existing process was used to harass legitimate patent owners while still being too unwieldy to serve as a practical alternative to litigation; reforms should balance ease of initiation with timeliness and effectiveness so administrative review can substitute for costly litigation where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTO fee-setting authority and reserve fund
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorize the Patent and Trademark Office to set and adjust fees to reflect actual costs and create a PTO reserve fund for fees collected above appropriations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Giving the PTO authority over fees, including a 15 percent surcharge and fast-track fees, enables it to reduce backlog by ensuring it has resources to carry out its mandates. The Administration emphasized the PTO must have timely access to fees collected to serve users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fast-track tools and fee discounts for priority technologies and small entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide tools to fast track applications and continue discounts for fast-tracked applications requested by small businesses and for technologies important to national competitiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fast-track procedures and discounts help true inventions issue more quickly, aid small businesses, and prioritize technologies important to the nation or economy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expanded prior user rights during transition
rubrics_metrics.description: Include an expanded prior user right alongside the transition to a first-inventor-to-file system to protect entities that commercially used an invention prior to the effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior user rights are particularly important for American manufacturing; the House bill included an expanded prior user right to address those concerns during the transition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation of prior art should rely on public records, not private activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Make validating prior art dependent on publicly accessible information rather than private activities or secret documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reduces opportunities to invent fake private prior-art claims and minimizes costly discovery to uncover private dealings; it increases predictability because public events are easier and cheaper to establish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection against theft via inventor public disclosure and filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a U.S. inventor publicly discloses or files an application, subsequent third-party applications filed after that date cannot validly defeat the inventor's rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This makes it harder for thieves (domestic or foreign) to obtain U.S. patents by alleging earlier conception. The inventor need not prove derivation of later filings; the filing/publication date secures priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application counts as section 103 prior art as of its filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application will constitute section 103 prior art as of its filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a result, a third party’s patent for a trivial or obvious variation filed after the provisional's filing date will be invalid and will not crowd out the original inventor's patent rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevention of fraudulent backdating of priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish priority dates based on government-filed documents (filings) rather than private records to prevent fraudulent backdating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the priority date will depend on a public government document, there is no opportunity to fraudulently backdate priority using privately held files, reducing disputes over invention dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrict false-marking litigation to parties with actual competitive injury
rubrics_metrics.description: Reform the false marking statute so suits can be brought only by parties who have actually suffered competitive injury as a result of false marking, and repeal the qui tam cause of action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents nuisance suits brought by parties (often lawyers) asserting no real injury and seeking $500 per product penalties; allows U.S. enforcement where appropriate and reduces frivolous litigation that imposes a 'tax' on manufacturing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve access to courts while creating administrative alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: While creating improved administrative mechanisms (postgrant review, reexamination), ensure that no party’s access to court is denied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reforms are designed to offer cost-effective alternatives to litigation but should not foreclose the ability of parties to seek judicial relief when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve patent quality to incentivize innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Raise the overall quality of patents issued by the PTO so that patents properly confer limited monopoly rights that incentivize inventors without impeding innovation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Low-quality patents undermine the value of patents and can impede innovation; measures such as third-party comments, postgrant review, and better PTO resources are intended to increase certainty and investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce the PTO application backlog
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the PTO has the resources and procedural tools to work through a large backlog of pending applications so true inventions can issue in a timely fashion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorizing fee adjustments, creating reserve funds, and providing fast-track tools are means to reduce delays (the record cites nearly 700,000 pending applications) and speed commercialization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmonize U.S. patent practice with international first-to-file systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Move the U.S. toward the first-inventor-to-file system used throughout the rest of the world to reduce confusion and inefficiencies for companies filing globally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Harmonization reduces costs for U.S. companies operating internationally and aligns U.S. practice with global patent norms, making it easier to protect inventions abroad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make post-grant and administrative review viable alternatives to costly litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide effective, timely post-grant and administrative review mechanisms so validity challenges can be resolved without resorting to protracted district-court litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A more usable administrative review process (as opposed to the prior, flawed inter partes reexamination) should serve as a realistic alternative to litigation, reducing time and expense in resolving patent disputes.
